tagline: The mid-engined Porsche that helped keep the company going.

issues.title: IMS Bearing Failure
issues.symptoms: Metallic debris in oil, grinding noise from engine, sudden catastrophic engine failure, oil light flickering
issues.description: The intermediate shaft (IMS) bearing supports the shaft that drives the camshafts, and when it fails, metal debris goes through the engine and usually ends it. Risk depends on the bearing: 1997–99 cars have a stronger dual-row bearing with a failure rate around 1%, while 2000–04 cars have a single-row bearing with a reported rate closer to 8%. A retrofit bearing, usually done with the clutch and rear main seal, takes the worry away.
fixes: Proactive IMS bearing replacement with upgraded bearing
LN Engineering ceramic hybrid bearing (most popular upgrade)
Plain bearing conversion (eliminates bearing entirely)
Regular oil analysis to detect early bearing wear
Use quality oil and change every 5,000 miles

repairCosts.notes: Preventive, and worth it. Usually done with the clutch and RMS.

issues.title: Rear Main Seal (RMS) Leak
issues.symptoms: Oil drips from bell housing area, oil on clutch (manual), burning oil smell, oil consumption
issues.description: The M96 rear main seal is known to weep, and on higher-mileage cars it can leak enough to contaminate the clutch. Because it sits between the engine and gearbox, replacing it means pulling the transmission, which makes it an obvious job to combine with an IMS retrofit and a clutch.
fixes: Replace rear main seal (requires engine/trans separation)
Combine with IMS bearing and clutch if applicable
Use updated Porsche seal (improved design)
Inspect flywheel for oil contamination damage

repairCosts.notes: Transmission out. Combine it with the IMS and clutch.

issues.title: Coolant Pipe Failure
issues.symptoms: Sudden coolant loss, overheating, coolant smell, puddle under car, white smoke from engine bay
issues.description: The cooling system runs a long way from the radiators in the nose to the engine behind the seats, and its plastic pipes, fittings, and expansion tank get brittle with heat and age. A cracked part can dump coolant quickly, so watch the level and fix small leaks before they become big ones.
fixes: Replace with updated oem plastic pipes
Upgrade to aluminum coolant pipe kit (permanent fix)
Replace coolant tank and hoses at the same time
Consider replacing thermostat during service
This is a preventive maintenance item—don't wait for failure

repairCosts.notes: Aluminum replacements are available for the plastic parts that fail.

issues.title: Convertible Top Issues
issues.symptoms: Top won't open/close, warning light on dash, hydraulic fluid leak, slow operation, top stops mid-cycle
issues.description: The top is electro-hydraulic. The pump, hydraulic rams, and the microswitches that tell the system where the top is are the usual failures, and a stuck top is often just a switch.
fixes: Check and refill hydraulic fluid (use correct Pentosin chf 11S)
Replace hydraulic rams if leaking
Replace or repair hydraulic pump
Adjust or replace micro switches
Replace top transmission if cables are worn
Regular lubrication of moving parts prevents issues

repairCosts.notes: Microswitches and the pump are the common failures.

issues.title: AOS (Air/Oil Separator) Failure
issues.symptoms: Rough idle, smoke from exhaust on startup, oil consumption, whistling noise, check engine light
issues.description: The air/oil separator strips oil from the crankcase vapors before they go back into the intake. When its diaphragm fails, the engine pulls oil into the intake: you'll see a cloud of smoke on startup, rising oil consumption, and a rough idle from the vacuum leak.
fixes: Replace AOS unit (oem or aftermarket)
Consider upgraded AOS designs that are more durable
Replace vacuum lines while AOS is accessible
Check and clean throttle body during service
Combine with other under-intake repairs to save labor

repairCosts.notes: Smoke on startup and oil consumption are the tell.

issues.title: Bore Scoring / Cylinder Wear
issues.symptoms: Knocking noise from engine (cold or hot), increased oil consumption, smoke on startup, low compression
issues.description: Some M96 engines score their cylinder walls, which lets oil past the rings. The exact cause is still debated. It ranges from minor to rebuild-the-engine, and the tell-tales are a ticking cold start, oil consumption, and sooty tailpipes on one bank. A borescope inspection before you buy is cheap insurance.
fixes: Borescope inspection to assess cylinder condition
For minor scoring: monitor and use quality oil
For severe scoring: cylinder sleeve repair or engine rebuild
LN Engineering offers cylinder repair services
Prevention: regular driving, proper warm-up, quality oil

repairCosts.notes: Major engine work: sleeving or a replacement engine.

issues.title: Window Regulator Failure
issues.symptoms: Window drops into door, grinding noise, slow window operation, window off track
issues.description: The regulators use cables and plastic parts that fail, so the window drops or moves erratically. The frameless glass also has to be adjusted correctly to seal against the top.
fixes: Replace window regulator assembly
Lubricate window tracks to reduce regulator strain
Check and adjust window alignment after replacement
Replace both sides if one fails (the other is likely close behind)

repairCosts.notes: Frameless glass needs proper adjustment afterward.

guides.title: Complete Suspension Refresh
guides.description: Front struts, the multi-link rear, and every bushing in between. Restores the handling that makes a Boxster a Boxster.
steps: Raise vehicle and support on jack stands at all four corners.
Remove all wheels and photograph suspension for reference.
Soak all suspension bolts with penetrating oil—let sit 15 minutes.
Begin with front suspension—remove sway bar end links.
Remove tie rod end nut (52 ft-lbs spec) and separate from knuckle using puller.
Remove control arm bolts at crossmember (48 ft-lbs spec).
Remove ball joint from steering knuckle—may require separator.
For struts: mark camber position, remove upper mount nuts, remove strut pinch bolt (74 ft-lbs).
Use spring compressor to disassemble strut—replace mount/bearing.
Install new front components—torque control arm to crossmember 48 ft-lbs.
Torque tie rod end to 52 ft-lbs with new cotter pin if castle nut.
For rear suspension: support rear trailing arm before removing bolts.
Remove upper and lower control arm bolts (63 ft-lbs spec).
Press new bushings into trailing arm if replacing.
Install new control arms—torque at ride height.
Replace rear sway bar end links.
Check wheel bearings for play—replace if worn.
Install wheels and lower vehicle—bounce corners to settle.
Professional alignment mandatory—the 986 is sensitive to alignment.
tips: The 986 uses non-serviceable control arm bushings—replace entire arm.
Front control arm ball joints are integrated—no separate replacement.
Check spring perches for cracks (common issue) while components are accessible.
Consider upgraded polyurethane bushings for sharper handling.
The mid-engine layout means the rear suspension has more effect on stability.
warnings: Spring compressors can be lethal if improperly used—follow instructions exactly.
Never strike ball joints directly—use proper separator tools.
The 986 is sensitive to alignment—incorrect specs cause poor handling.
Support the rear suspension properly—the engine is behind it.
Check for cracked spring perches before reassembly—safety item.

guides.title: Rust Prevention and Inspection
guides.description: The 986 is mostly rust-resistant, but clogged drains and water intrusion can still cause trouble. Where to look.
tools: Angle grinder with flap disc (if repairs needed)
steps: The 986 is galvanized and generally rust-resistant, but inspection is important.
Clean undercarriage thoroughly before inspection.
Inspect the front trunk area (frunk) for water intrusion—check drain tubes.
Check battery box area in front trunk—acid causes accelerated corrosion.
Inspect rocker panels by tapping with screwdriver—soft spots indicate rust.
Check door bottoms by opening doors fully and looking at drain holes.
Examine convertible top drain tubes—clogs cause interior water damage.
Open rear trunk and check around spare tire well for water accumulation.
Inspect engine compartment seams for corrosion from salt/debris.
Check suspension mounting points for any corrosion.
For surface rust: wire brush to bare metal, apply rust converter.
Prime with epoxy primer, then topcoat.
For rust-through (rare): cut and weld patch panels.
Apply cavity wax to all hollow sections—rocker interiors, frame rails.
Clear all drain holes and tubes with compressed air.
Ensure trunk seals are intact—water leaks cause electrical problems.
Document condition for future reference.
tips: 986s are generally rust-free due to galvanization—most issues are drain-related.
Front trunk water leaks damage the DME (engine computer)—a serious problem.
Convertible top drains clog with debris—clear them regularly.
Battery acid in the frunk causes the most common corrosion issues.
Annual Fluid Film application provides excellent protection.
warnings: Water in the front trunk can destroy expensive electronics.
Don't ignore clogged drains—water damage is expensive to repair.
Battery acid is corrosive—neutralize with baking soda solution.
Always wear respirator when grinding rust.
Fire extinguisher must be accessible if welding.

guides.title: Electrical System Service
guides.description: Coils, sensors, the top's electronics, and keeping water away from the DME.
steps: Begin with diagnostic scan to identify stored fault codes.
Check for water intrusion in front trunk—the DME lives there.
Clear front trunk drains if water is present.
For ignition coil replacement: open engine lid for access.
Disconnect coil electrical connectors, remove mounting bolts.
Remove coils and inspect spark plug wells for oil (valve cover gasket leak).
Install new coils, apply dielectric grease to boots.
For MAF sensor: located in air intake tube—two screws to remove.
Clean MAF element with MAF-specific cleaner only—no contact.
For O2 sensors: access from below on exhaust pipes.
Use O2 sensor socket and penetrating oil—threads can be seized.
Apply anti-seize to new sensor threads.
For window regulator: remove door panel and vapor barrier.
Support glass with tape, unbolt regulator, install new unit.
For convertible top issues: check hydraulic fluid level first.
Inspect microswitches at pivot points—common failure item.
Clean all ground points with wire brush, apply dielectric grease.
Clear fault codes and verify repairs.
tips: Many 986 electrical issues trace to water damage in the front trunk.
The DME (engine computer) is located in the frunk—protect it from water.
Frameless windows require precise adjustment after regulator replacement.
Convertible top issues are often just low hydraulic fluid.
A Durametric or PIWIS scanner provides far more diagnostic info than generic OBD2.
warnings: Water in the frunk can destroy the DME—several thousand dollars to replace.
Never use brake cleaner or carburetor cleaner on MAF sensors.
Convertible top microswitches can cause top to stop mid-cycle—dangerous.
Always disconnect battery before electrical work.
Support window glass before removing regulator—it will fall.

guides.title: Interior Restoration
guides.description: Leather, the convertible top, and the common wear items.
tools: Torx driver set (T15, T20, T25, T30)
steps: Document condition with photos before starting.
For leather: clean thoroughly with dedicated leather cleaner.
Address leather cracks with filler, sand smooth, apply dye.
Condition all leather surfaces—seats, door panels, dash.
For convertible top fabric: clean with top-specific cleaner.
Inspect for tears, worn spots, or separation at seams.
Treat fabric with protectant to prevent UV damage.
Check rear window for cloudiness or cracks (especially 1997-2002).
Replace rear window if cracked—heat gun removal from track.
Inspect and service convertible top mechanism—lubricate pivots.
Check hydraulic fluid level in reservoir (rear of car).
For worn shift/e-brake boots: pry out old boot, press new one in.
Replace cabin air filter—located behind frunk carpet.
Clean HVAC vents with detailing brushes.
Address any sticky interior surfaces with appropriate cleaner.
Apply UV protectant to all exposed surfaces.
Test all interior functions: windows, mirrors, locks, top.
tips: The 986's leather responds well to proper conditioning.
Early plastic rear windows crack easily—glass upgrade available.
Convertible top hydraulic fluid level is often overlooked—check it.
Lubricate top mechanism pivot points every 6 months.
Sport seats have aggressive bolsters that wear faster on driver side.
warnings: Never operate convertible top when wet or below freezing.
Use only top-specific cleaners—household products can damage fabric.
Don't use silicone-based products on leather.
Be careful with trim clips—they become brittle with age.
Rear window removal requires care to avoid damaging the track.

guides.title: IMS Bearing Retrofit (with Clutch and RMS)
guides.description: The fix most 986 owners choose: replace the intermediate shaft bearing with a stronger retrofit, and do the clutch and rear main seal at the same time since the transmission is already out.
tools: Retrofit installation tool kit (rent or buy)
steps: Raise the car securely and remove the transmission.
Remove the clutch and flywheel.
Lock the camshafts and crankshaft with the correct tools before touching the IMS.
Remove the IMS cover and inspect the old bearing. Save it for inspection if you're curious about its condition.
Remove the old bearing with the kit's tools and install the retrofit bearing per the kit instructions.
Refit the IMS cover with new seals.
Install a new rear main seal.
Install the flywheel and new clutch. Torque to the value in the Torque Specs table on this page, or your workshop manual.
Refit the transmission, remove the locking tools, and rotate the engine by hand before starting.
Change the oil and cut open the filter after the first few hundred miles.
tips: Some engines use a bearing that can't be removed without splitting the case. Check your engine number with the kit maker before you order.
An oil sample before and after the job tells you a lot about the engine's health.
warnings: If the cams aren't locked, the timing can jump when the IMS is disturbed.
Metal in the old filter or on the magnetic plug means stop and investigate before retrofitting.

diyGuides.title: Oil Change
diyGuides.description: Oil and filter on the M96. Short oil change intervals are cheap insurance on this engine.
tools: Ramps or jack and jack stands
steps: Warm the engine for 2-3 minutes—warm oil drains better.
Drive onto ramps or raise and support the car safely.
Locate the oil drain plug on the bottom of the engine.
Position drain pan and remove the 19mm drain plug.
Allow oil to drain completely—at least 10 minutes.
The spin-on oil filter is located under the car near the oil pan.
Using filter wrench, remove the old filter.
Important: Cut open the old filter and inspect for metal debris (IMS warning).
Apply fresh oil to the new filter's gasket.
Thread new filter on by hand until seated, then 3/4 turn more.
Replace the copper crush washer on the drain plug.
Reinstall drain plug and torque to 37 ft-lbs (50 Nm).
Add 8.5-9 quarts of 0W-40 or 5W-40 synthetic oil.
Start engine and check for leaks.
Check level after 2 minutes and top off as needed.
tips: Important: Cut open and inspect oil filter for metal debris—early IMS warning sign.
Frequent oil changes (every 5,000 miles) help protect the IMS bearing.
Use quality synthetic oil meeting Porsche A40 specification.
Consider periodic oil analysis to monitor engine wear.

diyGuides.title: Convertible Top Maintenance
diyGuides.description: Clean and lube the top's mechanism and seals so it keeps working and keeps the water out.
steps: Lower the convertible top fully to access all mechanism areas.
Inspect the hydraulic rams for any signs of leaking fluid.
Locate the pivot points on the top mechanism links.
Apply white lithium grease to all pivot points and hinges.
Lubricate the guide rails where the top slides.
Apply silicone spray to the rubber seals (top perimeter).
Inspect the fabric for any tears, wear spots, or loose stitching.
Check the rear window for delamination or cracks.
Operate the top up and down 2-3 times to distribute lubricant.
Wipe away excess lubricant that could attract dirt.
Check hydraulic fluid level in the reservoir if accessible.
Verify both microswitches are working (top should stop at endpoints).
tips: Don't operate the top if it's wet or below freezing.
A slow-operating top often means low hydraulic fluid.
The hydraulic pump is in the rear storage compartment.
Use Pentosin chf 11S for any hydraulic fluid top-off.

diyGuides.title: Brake Pad Replacement
diyGuides.description: Pads on the Brembo calipers, front and rear.
steps: Loosen lug bolts while car is on the ground.
Raise and support the car safely on jack stands.
Remove wheel to access caliper.
Disconnect brake pad wear sensor if equipped.
Remove the two 7mm Allen caliper guide pin bolts.
Swing the caliper up and support it—don't let it hang by the hose.
Remove the old pads from the caliper bracket.
Inspect rotor for scoring, cracks, or minimum thickness.
Clean pad contact surfaces with wire brush and brake cleaner.
Open brake fluid reservoir, then compress caliper piston.
Apply brake grease to pad backing plate contact points.
Install new pads—wear sensor slot goes on the inner pad.
Swing caliper down and reinstall guide pins to 22 ft-lbs (30 Nm).
Reconnect wear sensor.
Reinstall wheel and torque lugs to 96 ft-lbs (130 Nm).
Repeat for all corners.
Pump brake pedal until firm before driving.
tips: The 986 uses Brembo four-piston calipers on S models.
Open reservoir cap before compressing pistons.
Bed new pads with moderate stops—avoid hard braking initially.
Consider upgrading to ceramic pads for less brake dust.

diyGuides.title: Spark Plug Replacement
diyGuides.description: Plugs on the M96. Tight access, but doable in an hour.
steps: Allow engine to cool completely.
Open the engine lid for access.
The M96 has 6 spark plugs—accessed from the top of the engine.
Remove the coil packs by disconnecting connectors and removing bolts.
Use compressed air to blow debris from the spark plug wells.
Using spark plug socket and extension, remove each plug.
Inspect old plugs for wear, fouling, or damage.
Check plug gap on new plugs—should be 0.7-0.8mm.
Hand-thread new plugs to avoid cross-threading.
Torque plugs to 18-22 ft-lbs (25-30 Nm).
Apply dielectric grease to coil pack boots.
Reinstall coil packs and connect wiring.
Start engine and verify smooth operation.
tips: Use ngk or Bosch platinum/iridium plugs.
The 986 uses coil-on-plug ignition—no plug wires.
Inspect coil boots for cracks while replacing plugs.
Replace coils if you're experiencing misfires.

buyersGuide.overview: The Boxster helped keep Porsche afloat in the late '90s, and it handles the way a mid-engined car should. Its M96 engine shares the 996's known problems: the intermediate shaft (IMS) bearing, rear main seal leaks, and bore scoring on some engines. That's also why they're so cheap. Buy one with IMS paperwork, or budget for the retrofit, and you'll have one of the best-handling cars you can get at this price.

quickFacts.bestYears: 2003–2004 (facelift: glass rear window, updated interior). The 1997–99 cars have the stronger dual-row IMS bearing.

variants.name: Boxster (Base)
variants.description: The base car, with a 2.5L (1997–99) or 2.7L (2000–04) flat-six making 201–228 hp. Handles beautifully, with adequate power.

variants.name: Boxster S
variants.description: The 3.2L with 250–258 hp, bigger brakes, and bigger wheels. The one I'd buy.

items.detail: The big one. Intermediate shaft bearing can fail catastrophically. Check if upgraded or get oil analysis.
items.costIfBad: $2,000-3,500 for retrofit / Engine if it fails

items.detail: Rear main seal leak can indicate starting IMS bearing failure. Check for oil at bell housing.
M96 engines can develop cylinder bore scoring. Listen for knocking, check for smoke and oil consumption.
Check expansion tank for cracks, radiators for leaks. Overheating destroys engines.
Test full operation multiple times. Check hydraulic cylinders and cables.
Common failure. Test both windows multiple times up and down.
Plastic rear window yellows and scratches. Check visibility.
Clogged drains cause water in cabin. Check carpets for moisture.
Test every gear. The five-speed is tough, but check for synchro wear.
Check for smooth shifts. Less desirable but functional.
Should engage smoothly mid-travel. Mid-engine car makes clutch replacement easier than 911.
Wear causes clunking and vague handling. Common wear item.
Common failure causing misfires. Usually replaced in sets.
Dirty MAF causes running issues. Can often be cleaned.

The mid-engine layout gives it better balance than a 911 of the same era.
An IMS retrofit is worthwhile insurance. Factor it into the price.
The Boxster S is worth the extra money.
An oil analysis before you buy can hint at the IMS bearing's health.
If you do your own work, running costs are very reasonable for a Porsche.
Rennlist and Planet-9 both have excellent 986 sections.
The convertible top is dependable when the switches and seals are looked after.
Budget for a water pump and top maintenance.
